LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 4.1.1 PUBLIC SPEAKING – IMPROMPTU SPEECH

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 4
Topic 4.1: Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Public speaking – Impromptu speech
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Public speaking – Impromptu speech, part of Strand 4 in Grade 8 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do non- verbal cues enhance understanding? 2. Why is it important to follow the appropriate steps of first aid in case of an accident?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. watch and listen to a video recording of a story on safety at school,

2. identify the non-verbal cues (e.g. gestures, facial expressions, movement) used in presentation of the story,

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. watch and listen to a video recording of a story on safety at school,
2. identify the non-verbal cues (e.g. gestures, facial expressions, movement) used in presentation of the story,

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 4.1.1 Public speaking – Impromptu speech together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: The learner is motivated to learn continuously when they visit an institution that provides first aid

services and listens keenly to a talk on how to give first aid in case of an emergency.

• Self-efficacy: This is promoted as the learner shows concerted attention when conducting a discussion in clubs and societies

on safety measures to be taken in school to avoid accidents.

Values:
• Unity: This is enhanced as the learner cooperates with peers to discuss how the cues help to enhance understanding in

speaking.

• Love: This is promoted as the learner shows compassion by conducting a discussion forum in clubs and societies on safety

measures to be taken in school to avoid accidents.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Disaster Risk Reduction: This is promoted as the learner gets tips on how to appropriately administer first aid from practitioners

for safety in school.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of non-verbal cues to their learning of similar concepts in English.
